High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Baboo Ji
Chourasia - Advocate for appellant.

Shri Amit Pandey - Government Advocate for State Shri Shivam
Gautam - Advocate for objector.

Heard on I.A. No.10854 of 2024 which is first application under Section 389(1) of Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973 for suspension and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellant - Laxmi.

2.  The appellant has been convicted under Sections 376-D of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years with fine of Rs.2,000/- with default stipulation vide judgment dated 08.11.2023 passed by Third Additional Sessions Judge, District Chhatarpur in S.T. No.292/2014.
3.

entities.text: Third Additional Sessions Judge, District Chhatarpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: According to prosecution, in the night of 25.10.2014, prosecutrix was staying along with Vimla and Saroj in a Dharamshala located at Jatashankar Bus Stand, Chhatarpur; prosecutrix was having an headache for which Saroj gave her some medicine which made her semi-conscious; after some time, appellant and three more male persons came inside the room; the prosecutrix called for help but both the ladies who were accompanying her were not inside there; all the four male persons committed rape with her; next day she reported the matter in the Police Station Shahgarh upon which Crime No.06/2014 was registered.
After the conclusion of investigation and 2 CRA-497-2024 trial, appellant was convicted and sentenced.

4. The grounds raised in this application are that appellant was falsely implicated in the case,
prosecutrix was allegedly in unconscious state and the crime was committed in the darkness of room still she named the appellant in the FIR which was lodged with the delay; the prosecutrix herself was involved in series of criminal activities including the business of fake currency and there was no internal or external injury found on her body.
A compromise application was filed by her before the trial Court and the appellant was not ready for it, still this fact speaks about the false accusation made against the appellant.
5. The bail application has been opposed by the State on the ground that the DNA report received in the case has confirmed the involvement of appellant in the alleged crime.
6. Both the counsel have been heard.

sentences.text: 7. The DNA report received in the case has been marked as Exhibit- P24 and it reveals that the male choromosome genetic marker found on the source of prosecutrix was exactly similar for the blood samples of all the four male convicts.
Admittedly, all these male convicts are not real brothers and therefore, the learned counsel for the appellant has expressed doubt on the reliability of DNA report.

8. Taking into consideration the argued fact and also the other evidence available on record, but without commenting on the merits of the 3 CRA-497-2024 case, we are of the considered opinion that the application for suspension sentence moved on behalf of appellant deserves to be allowed.

9. It is directed that subject to depositing fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing personal bond by appellant in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, the execution of custodial part of his jail sentence shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail till the final disposal of this appeal.

The appellant after being enlarged on bail, shall mark his presence before the Registry of this Court on 13.01.2025 and on all such subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Registry of this Court in this regard.
10. Accordingly, I.A. No.10854 of 2024 is allowed and disposed of.
11. List for final hearing in due course.
